text:
maria.g: FYI customer AcmeCorp reporting massive tail latency and unexpected hosted charges. They were pinned to eu-west-1 dedicated but traffic spiked to hosted in us-west-2.

kai.ops: ugh. do we have request ids?

maria.g: yes — customer pasted one: req_id=01F9Y2Z8QX3, header X-Redwood-Target-Region: eu-west-1. Response had headers: X-Redwood-Routed-Pool: hosted-us-west-2, X-Redwood-Fallback: true, x-request-duration-ms: 1840

liz-prod: that duration explains the complaint. they hit ~1.8s token latency. customer says "we pay for dedicated capacity" and see hosted billing line items.

support-bot: Created incident INC-2026-2346 and attached logs.

kai.ops: quick theory — dedicated pool in eu-west-1 hit capacity and we allowed fallback, but fallback selector ignores region affinity for some model variants. can you repro?

maria.g: i reproduced in staging: curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-..." \n  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"hello"}'

response headers: 
  X-Redwood-Routed-Pool: hosted-us-west-2
  X-Redwood-Fallback: true
  X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason: capacity_exhausted

maria.g: i also toggled pool reservation to 0 and requests stayed pinned correctly to hosted eu-west-1 when fallback disabled, so behavior changes when fallback allowed.

tyler-eng: tagging infra. @kai.ops i remember a routing change last week to let cross-region fallbacks pick nearest latency pool irrespective of customer pin. that was intentional for availability but should have respected "region_pin" attribute.

kai.ops: right — policy RFC 2026-09 added cross-region fallback to reduce errors during regional outages. seems we missed honoring customer_region_pin in the selector. fix path: short-term disable cross-region fallback for reserved tenants, long-term add region affinity weight.

liz-prod: customer also claims billing spike — they show hosted usage units for the same time window as reserved throughput. could be double-count? anyone know our billing attribution when fallback used?

billing-bot: When fallback occurs, usage is billed to whichever pool served tokens. Reserved commit is charged separately; hosted charges are additive. Not a system double-bill bug, but definitely surprising to customers.

maria.g: sent AcmeCorp a screenshot pointing to fallback behavior and proposed mitigation: disable fallback for their tenant and open a refund evaluation. they replied OK but want a permanent fix.

tyler-eng: repro steps for platform:
1) create dedicated pool eu-west-1 with small capacity (n_gpus=1)
2) set tenant region_pin=eu-west-1 and enable hosted fallback=true
3) saturate pool with concurrent requests (ab) or rwd-load tool
4) observe X-Redwood-Routed-Pool switching to hosted-us-west-2

kai.ops: logs showing selector decision snippet: 
```
selector: {candidate_pools: [dedicated-eu-1, hosted-eu-1, hosted-us-west-2],
 rules_applied: [capacity_check, latency_estimate, cost_weight],
 final_choice: hosted-us-west-2,
 reason: fallback_capacity_latency_score
}
```

kai.ops: note candidate_pools contained hosted-eu-1 but its latency_estimate was inflated due to stale probe, pushing us to us-west. fix: ensure locality multiplier overrides stale probe for region_pin tenants.

liz-prod: timeline request from AcmeCorp for refund. they have spike on 2026-03-16 14:02–14:12 UTC. can ops capture exact token counts and which pool served each request?

maria.g: attached their request ids and our internal logs to the incident.

kai.ops: action items:
- (now) disable cross-region fallback for tenants with region_pin until patch (kai/tyler)
- (next 48h) patch selector to apply strong region affinity weight and prefer same-region hosted pools before cross-region (tyler)
- (support) communicate mitigation to AcmeCorp and initiate refund eval (maria.g, liz-prod)
- (billing) produce detailed hosted token usage per tenant for the window (billing-bot)

tyler-eng: estimating patch ~1 day dev + QA then deploy to routing canary.

support-bot: INC-2026-2346 updated: mitigation enabled for tenant acme-corp at 2026-03-16T15:10:32Z.

maria.g: customer confirmed latency dropped after we disabled cross-region fallback and saw no more hosted-us-west-2 hits. they asked for a note in our docs about fallback semantics and billing.

kai.ops: agree — docs: "Fallback may route to any compatible pool unless tenant has region_pin; we will change to prefer same-region pools. Hosted charges apply to tokens served by hosted pools even when you have reserved capacity."

liz-prod: next steps: postmortem + action items tracked in INC-2026-2346, assign owners. i'll coordinate refund convo.

tyler-eng: will open PR for selector logic and include unit tests for region_pin behavior.

maria.g: thanks all, closing loop with customer later today. :white_check_mark:
